rationale: Own-site conditioning yields the higher Poisson moment to which the pathwise Lp compactness criterion is applied.
from_statement: Let H be bounded self-adjoint on l2(Z^3), with bounded deterministic hopping and iid real site variables of bounded support and bounded probability density rho, scaled by a fixed lambda>0. Delete x to obtain H^x and its hopping vector b_x, and put Gamma_x(E,eta)=eta+Im<b_x,(H^x-E-i eta)^(-1)b_x>. Fix 0<q<1 and an open interval I. If for each x and each compact interval J contained in I, sup_{0<eta<1} E integral_J Gamma_x(E,eta)^(-q)dE<infinity, then almost surely all site spectral measures restricted to I are absolutely continuous, with locally L^(1+q) densities, and chi_I(H)l2(Z^3) is contained in the absolutely continuous subspace. This is a conditional criterion; the moment bound is not established for the lattice Anderson model here. Nonzero spectral weight is a separate requirement.
to_statement: Let mu_omega be random positive Borel measures on R of mass at most one, I a bounded open interval, p>1, and eta_n a deterministic positive sequence decreasing to zero. Put P_omega,eta(E)=integral eta/((t-E)^2+eta^2)dmu_omega(t). If sup_n E integral_I P_omega,eta_n(E)^p dE<=C<infinity, then almost surely mu_omega restricted to I has an Lp density f_omega, and E integral_I |f_omega(E)|^p dE<=C/pi^p.

rationale: The atom has uniformly bounded first Poisson energy moment but is singular.
from_statement: For the positive probability measure mu=delta_0 and P_eta(E)=eta/(E^2+eta^2), integral_R P_eta(E)dE=pi for every eta>0 although mu is purely atomic; integral_R P_eta(E)^2 dE=pi/(2 eta). A uniform first energy moment does not imply absolute continuity.
to_statement: Rejected inference: a uniform first energy moment of a scalar Poisson transform, or a bounded density of the disorder-averaged spectral measure, implies almost-sure absolute continuity of the sample measures. This implication is false: delta_0 and the random scalar operator with uniform eigenvalue give exact counterexamples. A higher moment or another argument excluding sample singular mass is required.

rationale: An absolutely continuous expected spectral measure coexists with purely atomic measures in every sample.
from_statement: If S is Uniform[-1,1] and H_S is the scalar self-adjoint operator S, its sample spectral measure is mu_S=delta_S, but E mu_S has density (1/2)1_[-1,1]. For every real E and eta>0, E Im(S-E-i eta)^(-1)<=pi/2. Thus uniform expected first resolvent imaginary parts do not imply samplewise absolute continuity.

rationale: The deterministic perturbation estimate loses its lower bound as eta tends to zero and does not close the gap.
from_statement: For the six-neighbour lattice, H_lambda^x=H_0^x+lambda V^x with ||V^x||<=1, lambda>0 and z=E+i eta with eta>0, ||(H_lambda^x-z)^(-1)-(H_0^x-z)^(-1)||<=lambda/eta^2. With ||b_x||^2=6, the corresponding cavity escape widths differ by at most 6 lambda/eta^2. A free lower bound Gamma_0,x>=c>0 yields Gamma_lambda,x>=c/2 by this estimate only under the sufficient restriction eta^2>=12 lambda/c. This estimate supplies no uniform control as eta tends to zero at fixed positive lambda.

Let (Omega, F, mu) be a measure space and 1 <= p < infinity with conjugate exponent q = p/(p-1) (q = infinity when p = 1). For 1 < p < infinity the map g -> (f -> integral f g dmu) is an isometric isomorphism from L^q(mu) onto the dual space L^p(mu)^*, for ANY measure space. For p = 1 the same map from L^infinity(mu) onto L^1(mu)^* is an isometric isomorphism provided mu is sigma-finite (or, more generally, localizable); without such a hypothesis it can fail to be surjective. The dual of L^infinity is strictly larger than L^1 whenever L^infinity is infinite-dimensional: on ([0,1], Lebesgue) a Banach limit or a Hahn-Banach extension of the functional f -> lim_{x -> 0} f(x) from C[0,1] gives an element of (L^infinity)^* not represented by any L^1 function. So the duality chain (L^1)^* = L^infinity does NOT continue to (L^infinity)^* = L^1, and L^1 is not reflexive; L^p is reflexive exactly for 1 < p < infinity. [standard; e.g. Folland, Real Analysis, 2nd ed., Theorem 6.15]
1 <= p < infinity
for p = 1: mu sigma-finite (or localizable)
no hypothesis on mu for 1 < p < infinity

Let $\mu$ be a finite positive measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with Stieltjes transform $m(z) = \int \frac{d\mu(t)}{t - z}$, defined and analytic for $\operatorname{Im} z > 0$, with $\operatorname{Im} m(z) > 0$ there. Then for every $a < b$ that are continuity points of $\mu$, $\mu((a, b]) = \lim_{\eta \downarrow 0} \frac{1}{\pi}\int_a^b \operatorname{Im} m(x + i\eta)\,dx$, and if $\mu$ has a continuous density $f$ at $x$ then $f(x) = \frac{1}{\pi}\lim_{\eta \downarrow 0} \operatorname{Im} m(x + i\eta)$. The real part has the companion limit $\operatorname{Re} m(x + i\eta) \to \pi H_f(x) := \mathrm{PV}\int \frac{f(t)}{t - x}\,dt$ wherever $f$ is Hölder continuous, so the boundary value $\breve m(x) = \lim_{\eta\downarrow0} m(x + i\eta) = \pi H_f(x) + i\pi f(x)$ (Sokhotski-Plemelj). In particular two measures with the same Stieltjes transform on $\mathbb{C}^+$ coincide, and a sequence of probability measures converges weakly if and only if the Stieltjes transforms converge pointwise on $\mathbb{C}^+$ (to the transform of a probability measure).
mu a finite positive Borel measure on the real line
for the density statement: mu absolutely continuous with a density continuous at x; for the real-part statement: the density Hölder continuous near x

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Review the failure of perturbation theory and test a restricted version on a tree-like subgraph. Result: On the Bethe lattice a.c. spectrum is known (Klein; Aizenman-Warzel) because the self-consistent equation for the Green function has a stable solution; on Z^3 the corresponding equation is not closed. A known partial statement is that the disorder-averaged Green function has diffusive behaviour up to times lambda^{-2-delta} (Erdos-Salmhofer-Yau), which is the kinetic regime and does not reach the infinite-time statement. I tested the possibility of transferring the tree result through a spanning tree of Z^3: the operator restricted to a spanning tree is not the operator on Z^3, and removing the edges changes the spectrum non-perturbatively, so no transfer. No result; the problem is recorded as attempted with the explicit obstruction that the only tools proving a.c. spectrum are tree-specific. Obstruction: Absence of a closed self-consistency equation on Z^3; kinetic-regime results stop at finite times.
